errors.location: Section 6, equations (24)–(25) and the sentence claiming that Q_n converges uniformly to f
errors.description: The Gaussian scale and normalization make Q_n tend to zero as n increases, rather than approximate f. Thus this argument does not establish the stated approximation result.
errors.evidence: The manuscript defines c_n by 1/c_n = ∫_C exp(−|ζ|²/n) dA(ζ), so c_n = 1/(πn). Since χf is supported in |ζ|≤ε, for bounded z the exponential kernel tends uniformly to 1 on that support; hence Q_n(z, z̄)=O(1/n) and tends uniformly to zero. This cannot converge to a nonzero f.

errors.location: Example 3.9, equation (5) and the claim that X is compact
errors.description: The displayed set X is not compact, so it does not provide the stated example of a compact set whose disc hull is noncompact.
errors.evidence: The points (1, φ_k(1), 1/k) belong to X. The sequence φ_k(1) is bounded, so a subsequence converges to some b; the corresponding points converge to (1,b,0), which is not in X because every point displayed in (5) has third coordinate 1/k>0.

errors.description: The asserted formula for DH(X) includes points arising from the boundary Im z₂=0 of the second component, even though that component requires Im z₂<0. In particular, (3/2,1) is included by (9) but is not in DH(X).
errors.evidence: An attached disc whose boundary lies in the second component has |φ₂|=1 on the boundary, so φ₂ is either constant or a finite Blaschke product. A nonconstant finite Blaschke product takes the boundary around the full unit circle and cannot have boundary values only in Im z₂<0; thus φ₂ must be constant with Im φ₂<0. A disc attached to the first component has |φ₁|=1 on the boundary and therefore |φ₁|≤1 inside. Neither type can contain (3/2,1), although equation (9) includes it.

errors.location: Theorem 8.1 proof, first disc construction following equation (28)
errors.description: The stated condition defining A₁ does not ensure that the positive real λ required by the construction exists, so the claimed inclusion A₁⊂DH(A₀) is not proved by this construction.
errors.evidence: For C>3, p=(1,i,−2i) satisfies (28): Im(ω·conjugate(ξ₁)·ξ₂)=0, Re(...)=2≥|ξ₁ξ₂|²=1, and the size bounds hold. But the proof requires λ²=wz₁/z₂=−2, which has no positive real solution. Also p∉A₀, since −2i≠conjugate(1)·i=i.
